title: Adaptive-spectrum traffic shaping and quarantine primitives for rollout SDK
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Add first-class SDK + control-plane primitives to express 'spectrum' traffic shaping for model rollouts: fine-grained weight distributions (not just single % splits), quarantine buckets for anomalous traffic, and adaptive auto-rollback windows. This work provides endpoints and client helpers that are idempotent, permission-scoped, and observable so product teams can run complex canaries, multi-variant A/B experiments, and shadow traffic flows with automated rollback when health signals degrade.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane endpoints: start_spectrum_rollout, adjust_weights, snapshot_rollout, promote_snapshot, and abort_rollout exist and return stable idempotency tokens.
SDK helpers: client-side token generation, optimistic-reconcile helpers, and traffic descriptor builders are available in JS and Python SDKs.
Permissions: RBAC roles (rollout_admin, rollout_operator, rollout_auditor) enforced at endpoint-level. Audit entries written for all mutating actions.
Quarantine buckets: ability to route a bounded subset of traffic to a quarantined variant (by predicate) and automatically move traffic out if health metrics cross thresholds.
Auto-rollback: policy engine supports time-windowed decay, hysteresis, and requires manual promotion for rollouts where safety gates fail more than X times.
Idempotency: repeated create/adjust requests with same idempotency token are no-ops and return the canonical rollout state; token TTL documented.
Telemetry: per-rollout token tracing, per-route cost/latency breakdown, and health hook integrations visible in Console and linked to rollout snapshots.
End-to-end tests in CI exercising idempotency, permission denial, quarantine activation, and auto-rollback logic pass consistently.
implementation_plan: API: Define protobuf+REST contract for /rollouts/spectrum with verbs: POST /start, PATCH /weights, POST /snapshot, POST /promote, POST /abort. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rserver/pull/7821)
SDK: Add helpers: RolloutBuilder, IdempotentAction(token_ttl_ms=...), Reconciler.backfill from snapshots. Implement in two packages: js-sdk and py-sdk (PRs: js#421, py#150).
Control-plane: persist rollout documents with monotonic sequence and idempotency token index; add 'quarantine' field to traffic allocation schema.
Permissions: extend authz middleware to support 'rollout_scoped' resources and map to existing org/team routing policy. Update policy generator UI hooks.
Policy engine: extend existing rollout policy evaluator to support adaptive windows, hysteresis, and per-metric thresholds. Add feature flag to toggle conservative mode.
Console: Add a small UX card for 'spectrum rollouts' with realtime weight sliders and quarantine indicators (design stub: Figma link).
Docs: Confluence design doc and SDK guides. Update API reference and add runbook for rollback scenarios.
design_decisions: We standardize on idempotency tokens scoped to (org, route, action) and store canonical token state for 24 hours. This avoids global token collisions and keeps token validation fast.

Quarantine buckets are evaluated at the proxy level using the same predicate engine as shadowing to keep routing latency sub-2ms; we trade slightly higher proxy complexity for lower control-plane calls.
Adaptive rollback uses a combination of rolling percentile increases + a backoff multiplier; this is simpler than full causal inference and is conservatively safe for production.
We will not attempt multi-region cross-consistency in this phase; rollouts are per-region and cross-region coordination is deferred to a separate epic.
tradeoffs: Storing idempotency tokens for 24 hours increases DB footprint but simplifies client retry semantics. We accept ~0.5% extra storage for predictable behavior.
Proxy-level quarantine evaluation adds code paths in the dataplane; this increases maintenance surface but avoids added round-trips to control-plane for every request.
Conservative default thresholds reduce false positives but may delay detection of subtle regressions; we provide knobs for advanced users.
testing_plan: Unit tests for API contract and idempotency semantics.
Integration tests: simulate concurrent adjust_weights calls from multiple operators and verify monotonic reconcile behavior.
E2E test in staging: run a 3-variant spectrum rollout against canary workload and trigger synthetic latency/failure to validate auto-quarantine and rollback.
Chaos test: induce control-plane DB latency and ensure SDK helpers surface clear retryable errors and do not cause double-promote races.
Security test: validate RBAC enforcement using automated policy harness and record audit log entries for each mutating action.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the new endpoints and SDK helpers behind 'spectrum_rollout' flag.
Canary: enable for internal infra routes only (10% of internal traffic) for 48 hours while monitoring health hooks.
Gradual: open to engineering orgs with opt-in via Console templates, increase exposure to 25% then 50% across non-prod namespaces.
GA: enable for all orgs with default conservative thresholds and docs + runbook published. Provide a migration tool for existing legacy rollouts.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create rollout-specific metrics: rollout_success_rate, quarantine_activation_rate, rollback_count, idempotency_token_conflicts.
Dashboards: per-route spectrum view with weight history and snapshot timeline.
Alerts: notify SRE and rollout owners when quarantine_activation_rate > 0.5% over 5m or rollback_count > 3 in 1h.
Runbook: automated incident steps and escalation path documented in Confluence.
